{"obligations":{"reduction":{"status":"written_and_valid","quote":null,"witness":null,"load_bearing":null},"lower_bound":{"status":"written_but_invalid","quote":"Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree).","witness":"Counterexample: take q=2 with a_1=1/10 and a_2=9/10, and make one cut splitting a_2 into pieces 1/2 and 2/5. The sorted pieces are (1/2,2/5,1/10). The sole rank-pair consists of two pieces from vertex 2, so its edge is a loop. Thus the graph has one edge on two vertices, satisfying 1≤q−1 and having fewer edges than vertices, but it contains a loop; moreover the component containing a_q=a_2 is not a tree and cannot be bipartitioned as asserted.","load_bearing":"The tree claim is used to obtain the bipartition and inequality (3), which are the entire proof of D≥Γ for every Xiang refinement.
